pathway.title: RLJ Lodging Trust — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity is the strongest support and covers the near-term needs: cash of USD 448.34 million and the undrawn USD 600.00 million revolver give USD 1,048.34 million, which is 1.31 times the USD 800.00 million of term loans due in 2027 and 2028, and no principal is scheduled before 2027. Pro forma cash for the hotel sale on 2026-10-08 is not established, and revolver access depends on covenant compliance that the filings report only as met. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

Earnings are recovering but remain below FY2024 and fall faster than revenue when demand weakens: in FY2025 revenue fell 1.43% while property operating expenses rose 1.09%, and reported EBITDA fell 8.23%, a percentage fall 5.76 times that of revenue. In the first nine months of 2026 revenue rose 5.50% and reported EBITDA 5.26%, with RevPAR at comparable hotels up 7.04%, yet last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 329.07 million is still 4.52% below FY2024. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C7

Reported leverage has not fallen since FY2024 and cover is thin: net debt over reported EBITDA is 5.31x at 2026-09-30 against 5.25x at FY2024, because net debt fell 3.44% while EBITDA fell 4.52%, and the 5.04x pro forma for the sale on 2026-10-08 is lower only because the sale cash reduces net debt while the sold hotels' earnings stay in EBITDA. EBITDA covers cash interest 2.94 times, 2.40 times once the Series A preferred dividends are counted as a fixed charge, and 2.69 times if the FY2025 earnings decline repeated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C13; calculation C14

Refinancing capacity is adequate but its cost is rising: the 2026 refinancing left no principal due before 2027, yet it repaid the USD 500.00 million of 3.75% notes on 2026-07-01 mainly with floating-rate term loans costing 5.51% and 5.91% after hedges, and 76.2% of debt is variable, with 65.7% fixed or effectively fixed after swaps and caps. USD 689.40 million (31.22% of principal) falls due in 2029, and if both extension options on the USD 500.00 million 2027 term loan were used it would fall due in the same month as the USD 500.00 million 2029 notes, putting USD 1,000.00 million (45.28% of principal) in one month. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C16

Cash conversion supports distributions today, but the cushion has been thin: operating cash flow less capex of USD 181.78 million covered distributions of USD 117.10 million 1.55 times in the last twelve months, after covering them only 1.00 times in FY2025, when the common dividend had risen from USD 0.36 per share in FY2023 to USD 0.60 while operating cash flow fell 22.64%. Capex, cut 31.81% in the first nine months of 2026, is the main lever. The REIT rule to distribute at least 90% of taxable income limits retained cash, so debt at maturity must be refinanced and not repaid from cash flow. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 115; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; calculation C18; calculation C21

The structure favours unsecured creditors but their ranking is not established: only eight hotels are mortgaged, the revolver, term loans and 2029 notes are unsecured, and the Midway Airport hotels were sold for about 3.92% more than their net carrying value before costs, yet no filing states a legal rank among the unsecured facilities. The Series A preferred shares add USD 25.12 million of annual dividends and a liquidation value of USD 328.27 million, and the credit agreements count preferred dividends paid as a fixed charge. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 9–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C14; calculation C17

Governance and concentration are watch items and not constraints: no sponsor is named and seven of the nine trustees are stated to be independent, which corrects the Business & governance statement that trustee independence is not established. Against that, two managers run 51.09% of consolidated hotels, 83 of 93 hotels carry three brand families, and 60.84% of the nine-month revenue increase came from three markets. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 82; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

cells.text: The Trust is sole general partner of RLJ Lodging Trust, L.P. and owns 99.5% of its units; the operating partnership's subsidiaries own the hotels and lease 91 of 92 hotels at 2026-09-30 to taxable REIT subsidiary lessees, which engage independent managers
Creditor claims sit in the operating partnership and the hotel-owning subsidiaries; the Trust guarantees the senior notes
Rooms were 80.99% of FY2025 revenue, food and beverage 11.72% and other revenue 7.29%; for nine months 2026 the shares were 81.25%, 11.29% and 7.46%
Earnings follow occupancy and rate; the rooms-led, focused-service model keeps food and beverage and meeting exposure small

83 of 93 hotels at 2025-12-31 carry Marriott (35), Hilton (36) or Hyatt (12) brands; franchise royalties are 2.0% to 6.0% of room revenue plus 1.0% to 4.3% for marketing and reservations, and the Trust guarantees each franchise agreement
Brand standards drive capital spending, and termination for default or change of control would remove a hotel's brand

15 management companies run the 92 consolidated hotels at 2025-12-31; Aimbridge runs 26 and Hilton 21, together 51.09%; base management fees are 1.5% to 3.5% of hotel revenue and owners may terminate for missed performance targets
The owner controls little of daily operations, and a failure or dispute at one large manager reaches many hotels
Management and franchise fee expense was 7.61% of FY2025 revenue (management 39.0 and franchise 63.8, USD million); incentive fees are paid after a priority return to the owner
Fees come out of hotel revenue before owner cash flow and move with revenue, not with profit
The three largest markets (Northern California, Southern California, South Florida) produced 35.85% of FY2025 revenue and the two California markets 24.84%
Regional demand, hurricane and earthquake exposure and insurance cost matter more than portfolio size suggests

Reserve funding for furniture, fixtures and equipment is typically 4.0% to 5.0% of hotel revenue under management, franchise and mortgage terms; restricted cash reserves were USD 37.5 million at 2026-09-30
A fixed share of revenue is set aside before distributions, which supports hotel quality but ties up cash
Northeastern hotels earn less from December to March and Florida hotels more from January to April
Quarterly cash flow swings, so liquidity at one quarter end is not a run rate

runs.text: Liquidity is the strongest support. Cash and the undrawn revolver give USD 1,048.34 million, which funds the 2027 and 2028 term loans 1.31 times, and the 2026 refinancing pre-funded the notes due in 2026, so default probability over the next two years is low unless covenant compliance fails. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C1; calculation C2

The unsecured structure supports recovery for the unsecured debt: only eight hotels carry mortgage loans, the other hotels carry no mortgage, and the indenture and credit agreements test the unencumbered asset to debt ratio, so unsecured creditors keep access to most of the asset base, although their ranking among themselves is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13

The 2026 operating recovery and cash conversion support deleveraging: comparable RevPAR rose 7.04% for nine months, reported EBITDA rose 5.26%, and operating cash flow less capex covers distributions 1.55 times with capex that can be cut, so net leverage can fall if the recovery holds and the sale cash repays debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C7; calculation C9

Hedging and an interest-only profile bound the rate risk: 65.7% of debt is fixed or effectively fixed and a 100 bp rise on the rest costs about USD 7.9 million a year, which is 7.05% of last-twelve-months cash interest, so a rate shock would slow cover but not threaten it alone. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C11

Net leverage and cover are the main weakness. At 5.31x (5.04x pro forma for the 2026-10-08 sale) and 2.94 times they have not improved since FY2024, so an earnings decline moves leverage directly toward the covenant tests without a cushion that the filings let us measure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C4

Earnings are geared to RevPAR. A 1.43% revenue fall produced an 8.23% fall in reported EBITDA in FY2025, and Hotel EBITDA margin fell to 27.92% on a last-twelve-months basis from 30.34% in FY2023, so downside moves faster than the revenue line suggests. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 122–123; calculation C5; calculation C6

The 2027 to 2029 refinancing stack is the pressure point. The 2026 refinancing replaced 3.75% notes with term loans at 5.51% and 5.91%, USD 500.00 million of 4.00% notes follows in 2029, and extension options on the 2027 term loan would stack USD 1,000.00 million in one month, so higher coupons and market access decide the credit. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C12; calculation C16

Concentration reduces flexibility: two managers run 51.09% of hotels, three brand families cover 83 of 93 hotels and three markets supplied 60.84% of the 2026 revenue growth, so a single manager, brand or region event reaches cash flow broadly. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C8

Distribution policy outran cash flow in the downturn: the common dividend per share rose 66.67% from FY2023 to FY2025 while operating cash flow fell 22.64%, free cash flow after capex covered distributions only 1.00 times in FY2025, and Series A preferred dividends of USD 25.12 million are a fixed claim on top, so there was no cushion for a further decline until capex was cut in 2026. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation C14; calculation C21

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The February 2026 refinancing recast the Revolver to February 2030, upsized one term loan to USD 569.00 million, added a USD 150.00 million seven-year term loan and extended two mortgage loans to April 2029, at a cost of USD 14.00 million of lender fees and legal costs. During 2026 another previously unencumbered hotel was added to a mortgage loan for USD 23.40 million of extra proceeds, so the secured claim grew while unsecured maturities were pushed out. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 124; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

No bonds were issued in 2026: the 3.75% notes due 2026 were repaid at maturity on 2026-07-01 from the refinancing proceeds, and the next scheduled maturity after extension options is in 2029. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 11

After the quarter end the sale of seven hotels near Midway Airport closed on 2026-10-08 for about USD 110.00 million, of which about USD 90.00 million was cash and about USD 20.00 million was seller financing with a three-year term and one extension option; the buyer assumed the franchisors' key money obligations. The use of the cash is not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 25

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RLJ Lodging Trust (rlj-1511337), as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the issuer's business, ownership, operating model, corporate history and governance behaviour from the five supplied filings, building on the source readiness result.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The document dates are signature dates; for the two annual reports they match the filing dates that later filings name, and the filing dates of the quarterly reports are not stated in the supplied text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RLJ is a publicly held lodging REIT with no sponsor named, so creditors depend on diversified hotel cash flows run by third-party managers under a few brands, and protection comes from asset quality and mostly unsecured funding rather than from an owner's support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings document no owner extraction, creditor-adverse transaction or covenant relief: the common dividend was USD 0.60 per share in FY2025, three hotel sales raised USD 73.70 million and the 2026 refinancing extended maturities. Ownership percentages, board independence and the legal room to pay distributions are not established because the proxy statement and executed debt documents are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership is dispersed and no sponsor is named, so creditors have neither a sponsor to support them nor a sponsor whose extraction they must price, but percentage holdings by shareholder are not established. The Trust is the sole general partner of the operating partnership and owns 99.5% of its units, a small group of other limited partners holds the rest, and the annual report caps any holder at 9.8% of the shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flows are spread across many hotels but are concentrated in three brand families, two managers and a few markets: 83 of the 93 hotels at the end of 2025 carry Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt brands, Aimbridge and Hilton run 51.09% of the consolidated hotels, and the three largest markets produced 35.85% of FY2025 revenue, of which the two California markets produced 24.84%. A brand or manager dispute, or a California event, therefore reaches many hotels at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 105; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C3; calculation C2; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The owner has limited control over operations and fees come ahead of owner cash flow: independent managers control hotel operations, rooms generate 80.99% of revenue, and management and franchise fees took 7.61% of FY2025 revenue, while the Trust guarantees the obligations under each franchise agreement. Fee levels and brand standards therefore sit largely outside the owner's day-to-day control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 115; calculation C1; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Funding is mostly unsecured and guaranteed within the group, which leaves most hotels unencumbered: the annual report describes unsecured senior notes, unsecured credit agreements and mortgage loans secured by certain hotels, mortgage loans encumber eight hotels, and the senior notes carry the guarantee of the Trust and certain operating partnership subsidiaries. This module relies on that statement that the senior notes are unsecured; Financial foundation lists their security as not stated, and the annual report controls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has been measured and has recycled assets rather than added leverage: the common dividend was USD 0.60 per share in FY2025 and USD 0.45 per share for the first nine months of 2026, three hotels were sold for USD 73.70 million in 2025 and eight for USD 123.20 million in 2026, and USD 28.60 million of shares were repurchased in 2025 and none in the first nine months of 2026, under programmes that each authorise up to USD 250.00 million. The credit agreements restrict dividends only while an event of default exists and the indenture limits restricted payments on terms not supplied, so the payout looks like policy rather than a covenant constraint, but that is not tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but governance detail sits outside the supplied filings: the statements carry an auditor's report and quarterly reports follow, the board is a small group of trustees led by an executive chairman, trustees can be removed only for cause by a two-thirds vote, and covenant compliance is reported each period as met. Trustee independence, pay, committee roles and related-party dealings are in the proxy statement, which is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contractual claims on hotel cash flow beyond debt are modest but real: 12 consolidated hotels sit on ground leases, one of which expires in 2029 and would revert to the lessor if not extended, and restricted cash is reserved for capital spending under management, franchise and mortgage terms. These claims are fixed before owner cash flow and matter more when hotel earnings fall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a benign reading is that no sponsor or controlling holder stands behind creditors while distributions continue and buybacks are authorised: net income attributable to common shareholders fell from USD 42.91 million in FY2024 to USD 3.39 million in FY2025 and preferred dividends alone were USD 25.12 million, so the payout exceeds earnings and rests on operating cash flow, a new authorisation of USD 250.00 million is in place until May 2027, and the Trust has no cyber insurance while relying on managers' systems. The view would turn adverse if a repurchase or special distribution were funded with borrowing, if a mortgage cash trap or a covenant waiver appeared, if a manager or brand relationship ended across many hotels, or if the proxy statement showed concentrated holdings or related-party fees; it would turn favourable if the executed debt documents confirmed wide covenant headroom and tight limits on restricted payments.

fields.value: Earnings are recovering but remain below FY2024 and fall faster than revenue when demand weakens: in FY2025 revenue fell 1.43% while property operating expenses rose 1.09%, and reported EBITDA fell 8.23%, a percentage fall 5.76 times that of revenue. In the first nine months of 2026 revenue rose 5.50% and reported EBITDA 5.26%, with RevPAR at comparable hotels up 7.04%, yet last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 329.07 million is still 4.52% below FY2024.

fields.value: Reported leverage has not fallen since FY2024 and cover is thin: net debt over reported EBITDA is 5.31x at 2026-09-30 against 5.25x at FY2024, because net debt fell 3.44% while EBITDA fell 4.52%, and the 5.04x pro forma for the sale on 2026-10-08 is lower only because the sale cash reduces net debt while the sold hotels' earnings stay in EBITDA. EBITDA covers cash interest 2.94 times, 2.40 times once the Series A preferred dividends are counted as a fixed charge, and 2.69 times if the FY2025 earnings decline repeated.

fields.value: Refinancing capacity is adequate but its cost is rising: the 2026 refinancing left no principal due before 2027, yet it repaid the USD 500.00 million of 3.75% notes on 2026-07-01 mainly with floating-rate term loans costing 5.51% and 5.91% after hedges, and 76.2% of debt is variable, with 65.7% fixed or effectively fixed after swaps and caps. USD 689.40 million (31.22% of principal) falls due in 2029, and if both extension options on the USD 500.00 million 2027 term loan were used it would fall due in the same month as the USD 500.00 million 2029 notes, putting USD 1,000.00 million (45.28% of principal) in one month.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion supports distributions today, but the cushion has been thin: operating cash flow less capex of USD 181.78 million covered distributions of USD 117.10 million 1.55 times in the last twelve months, after covering them only 1.00 times in FY2025, when the common dividend had risen from USD 0.36 per share in FY2023 to USD 0.60 while operating cash flow fell 22.64%. Capex, cut 31.81% in the first nine months of 2026, is the main lever. The REIT rule to distribute at least 90% of taxable income limits retained cash, so debt at maturity must be refinanced and not repaid from cash flow.

fields.value: The structure favours unsecured creditors but their ranking is not established: only eight hotels are mortgaged, the revolver, term loans and 2029 notes are unsecured, and the Midway Airport hotels were sold for about 3.92% more than their net carrying value before costs, yet no filing states a legal rank among the unsecured facilities. The Series A preferred shares add USD 25.12 million of annual dividends and a liquidation value of USD 328.27 million, and the credit agreements count preferred dividends paid as a fixed charge.

fields.value: Governance and concentration are watch items and not constraints: no sponsor is named and seven of the nine trustees are stated to be independent, which corrects the Business & governance statement that trustee independence is not established. Against that, two managers run 51.09% of consolidated hotels, 83 of 93 hotels carry three brand families, and 60.84% of the nine-month revenue increase came from three markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate view is that operating leverage has already worn the margin down while debt stayed flat: Hotel EBITDA margin fell from 30.34% in FY2023 to 27.92% on a last-twelve-months basis, so a second decline like FY2025 would lift net leverage to 5.79x and cut cover to 2.69 times, or 2.52 times if floating rates also rose 100 bp, before any refinancing cost, and distributions were raised into the decline. The strongest evidence for a better view is that operating cash flow less capex would still cover distributions 1.21 times in that scenario with capex held at the last-twelve-months level, capex is flexible, the common dividend is set by the board, and liquidity is 1.31 times the term loans due by 2028.

fields.value: The view would improve if the USD 90.00 million of sale cash were used to repay debt and net leverage settled below the pro forma 5.04x, if RevPAR growth held through the 2027 term loan decision, or if the executed credit agreement showed wide covenant headroom. It would weaken if RevPAR growth turned negative for two quarters, if proceeds funded repurchases under the USD 250.00 million programme, if the 2027 term loan were refinanced at or above the 5.91% of the newest term loan, or if a covenant waiver or mortgage cash trap appeared.

fields.value: - Covenant tests are reported as met without ratio values, so the conclusion that the USD 600.00 million revolver is available for the 2027 and 2028 term loans rests on the issuer's statement and not on measured headroom; thin headroom would remove most of the liquidity this view relies on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management outlook, rating or traded price is supplied, so the downside scenario scales the FY2025 outcome and not a management plan, and refinancing access is judged from the issuer's own fair value estimate of USD 489.10 million for fixed-rate debt of USD 525.00 million, which is an estimate and not a quote.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No balance sheet follows the 2026-10-08 sale, so a pro forma net leverage of 5.04x assumes the USD 90.00 million of cash reduces net debt and keeps the sold hotels' earnings in EBITDA; if those hotels earned a positive EBITDA, the true pro forma ratio is higher.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating statistics cover comparable hotels only and exclude four hotels sold in 2025 and 2026, so the 7.04% RevPAR gain describes the retained portfolio, while total revenue growth of 5.50% is after USD 13.20 million less room revenue from the non-comparable hotels; the two rates are not like for like, and the recovery in the retained hotels is stronger than the total.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Hotel-level earnings and the finances of managers and franchisors are not disclosed, so the finding that diversification protects cash flow is measured by revenue spread and not by profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: RLJ Lodging Trust is a Maryland real estate investment trust that owned 92 hotels at 2026-09-30, mostly premium-branded, rooms-oriented hotels in urban markets, run by independent managers. Substantially all assets and liabilities sit in RLJ Lodging Trust, L.P., of which the Trust owns 99.5%, and 91 of the 92 hotels are leased to taxable REIT subsidiaries. Rooms produced 80.99% of FY2025 revenue, the customer base is mainly transient and group business that uses meeting space is a small part of it, so cash flow follows occupancy and room rates and no contracted revenue sits behind the debt. The spread across many hotels and travellers limits single-customer risk, but hotel-level earnings are not disclosed, so the spread is measured by revenue and not by profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 28; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor or controlling holder is named, and the Trust is the sole general partner of the operating partnership; the annual report limits any holder to 9.8% of the common shares unless the board agrees. Nine trustees signed the annual report, an executive chairman, a chief executive who is also a trustee and seven others, and the annual report states that seven trustees are independent; this corrects the Business & governance statement that trustee independence is not established, while pay, committee roles, related-party dealings and holdings by shareholder remain unsupplied. Financial policy was shareholder-friendly into the FY2025 decline and has been restrained in 2026: the common dividend per share rose from USD 0.36 in FY2023 to USD 0.50 in FY2024 and USD 0.60 in FY2025 while operating cash flow fell 22.64%, and USD 28.59 million of shares were repurchased in FY2025 alongside USD 69.04 million of hotel sale proceeds, whereas in the first nine months of 2026 the dividend was USD 0.15 per share in each quarter and no shares were repurchased under the USD 250.00 million authorisation. This refines the Business & governance reading of capital allocation as measured, which holds for 2026 and for leverage but is too favourable for FY2024 and FY2025 cash coverage. Creditor alignment is adequate on what was done, but it is not tested against the limits on restricted payments in the debt documents, which are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 20; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transient and cyclical, and corporate and government travel moved from drag to support between FY2025 and 2026. Room revenue at comparable hotels fell in FY2025 because international, government, corporate and group travel decreased, with RevPAR down 1.75% to USD 143.43, and rose in the first nine months of 2026 on leisure, corporate and government travel and renovated hotels returning, with RevPAR up 7.04% to USD 156.51 on occupancy of 74.4% and ADR of USD 210.32. Pricing power is present in 2026, with ADR up 4.49%, but it is not assured because competition can stop operators raising rates as fast as inflation. Northeastern hotels earn less from December to March and Florida hotels more from January to April, so one quarter-end balance is not a run rate. Revenue visibility is therefore short, and creditors rely on demand holding and not on contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2026 growth leaned on the three largest markets: Northern California, Southern California and South Florida produced 37.51% of nine-month 2026 revenue against 36.23% a year earlier and 60.84% of the USD 56.17 million revenue increase, with Northern California up 14.75%. A regional shock, such as the earthquake and hurricane exposure the annual report names, therefore reaches more of the recovery than the number of hotels suggests, which matters most for the 2027 refinancing decision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended only in part under volume pressure, and the evidence is the trend. Variable costs follow occupancy, management and franchise fees follow revenue (7.61% of FY2025 revenue), and the annual report states that a change in ADR moves operating margin more than a change in occupancy. In FY2025 property operating expenses rose 1.09% while revenue fell 1.43%, and Hotel EBITDA margin fell from 30.34% in FY2023 and 29.12% in FY2024 to 27.34% in FY2025, even though revenue rose 3.31% in FY2024; the margin is 27.92% on a last-twelve-months basis. In the first nine months of 2026 property operating expenses at comparable hotels rose USD 46.16 million against a USD 57.40 million rise in comparable room revenue, with wages and benefits cited first, while lower property insurance premiums cut property tax, insurance and other expense by USD 1.95 million. Cost flexibility sits mainly with independent managers: the Trust has limited ability to influence their staffing decisions and approval rights over key posts at many hotels, so creditors should expect the FY2025 sensitivity to return in a downturn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, pages 122–123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate and partly discretionary. Capex was USD 76.17 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 111.71 million a year earlier, which is 6.46% of last-twelve-months revenue against 9.36% in FY2025, while reserve funding of 4.0% to 5.0% of hotel revenue is required at some hotels under management, franchise and mortgage terms and USD 37.49 million of restricted cash was held for it at 2026-09-30. Interest is the largest contractual cash call at USD 112.06 million over the last twelve months; the notes and mortgage loans require interest only through maturity and the maturity table shows no principal before 2027. Operating cash flow less capex of USD 181.78 million covered distributions 1.55 times, although payables and other liabilities added USD 13.18 million more cash than a year earlier, so part of the 2026 improvement is working capital. Capex can be cut in a downturn, but brand standards and lender reserves limit how far.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C9; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high and local: the annual report describes the industry as highly competitive and market-specific, with competition from existing and new focused-service and compact full-service hotels, and comparable occupancy slipped to 71.6% in FY2025 from 72.7% before recovering to 74.4% for nine months 2026 against 72.6%. Rivalry contests rate growth and margin market by market, so it limits how fast earnings and cover can recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New supply is driven by construction cost and financing availability, and tariffs on construction materials and furniture raise renovation cost for existing owners, so the barrier to entry is cost and not regulation. No supply data are supplied, so the effect of new hotels on the markets with the most revenue is not established. Substitutes are non-traditional accommodations such as online home and apartment rentals, which the annual report names as competition for the same travellers and which cap rate growth at the price-sensitive end.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high on price and low on concentration: customers are mostly transient, group business is small, and no customer is named as material, so no single buyer can cut revenue, but guests and online channels compare rates freely. Supplier power is the force that matters most to creditors: independent managers run daily operations and take fees, franchisors set brand standards, fees were 7.61% of FY2025 revenue and the Trust guarantees each franchise agreement, so a dispute or termination at one large manager or brand reaches many hotels at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors are material through travel policy and taxes: the annual report ties demand to government spending and inbound international travel under visa policies, and FY2025 comparable room revenue fell in part because international and government travel decreased. The REIT rule to distribute at least 90% of taxable income is a financial constraint as well as a tax rule, because it pushes capital spending and maturities toward external financing. Economic factors are the main driver: inflation raises wages and renovation cost faster than rate growth can follow, and higher interest rates lift the cost of the 76.2% of debt that is variable. Technology is a secondary factor, but the Trust carries no cyber insurance and relies on managers' systems. Social factors are not a primary credit driver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-K_2025-12-31_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_rlj.htm.jsonl, page 42

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Credit-translated strengths: liquidity of USD 1,048.34 million with no principal before 2027; mostly unsecured funding with eight mortgaged hotels; interest-only debt with 65.7% fixed or effectively fixed; and a recovering earnings base with capex flexibility. Credit-translated weaknesses: net leverage of 5.31x (5.04x pro forma for the 2026-10-08 sale) and cover of 2.94 times that have not improved since FY2024; earnings that fall 5.76 times faster than revenue; a 2027 to 2029 maturity stack that must be refinanced at higher rates; and concentration in managers, brands and three markets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are limited to using sale proceeds to cut debt, continued RevPAR growth in the renovated hotels, and refinancing the 2027 term loan early on the extended terms of the newer facilities. Threats that could weaken it are a second fall in international, government and corporate travel, further tariff and wage inflation, a floating-rate reset on the unhedged share of debt, and repurchases or distributions funded with borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are liquidity, a mostly unsecured and interest-only debt stack and a 2026 operating recovery that has lifted nine-month reported EBITDA 5.26%. The main constraints are leverage that has not fallen, cover of 2.94 times, a margin that has lost about 2.42 percentage points of Hotel EBITDA margin since FY2023, and 76.2% variable-rate debt that is refinanced into higher coupons. Scale is a support, with 92 hotels, and so is the rooms-led model that keeps food and beverage and meeting exposure small. Free cash flow is stable enough to cover distributions in the base case but not strongly so: cover was 2.45 times in FY2023, 1.56 times in FY2024 and 1.00 times in FY2025, is 1.55 times in the last twelve months, and would be 1.21 times in the FY2025-type scenario with capex held low. Financial policy is average, because distributions were raised while cash flow fell and then held in 2026, and market access is adequate on the 2026 refinancing but not tested by prices or ratings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trend is flat on credit metrics and improving on operations. Debt is little changed at USD 2,196.33 million of carrying value, book debt is 46.47% of total assets against 46.33% at FY2025, and lease liabilities of USD 118.63 million sit outside the debt figure; including them would lift net leverage to 5.67x, which overstates it because reported EBITDA is already after ground rent. Twelve hotels are on ground leases with expense of USD 15.71 million in FY2025 and total future lease payments of USD 570.44 million at 2025-12-31, the largest rent being USD 5.04 million at the San Diego hotel whose lease expires in 2029. Key missing datapoints are covenant ratio values, ratings and traded prices, management guidance, hotel-level earnings and a post-sale balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the 2026 demand recovery (comparable RevPAR up 9.68% in the third quarter), renovated hotels still ramping, lower capex and USD 90.00 million of sale cash that can cut debt. The headwinds are the USD 500.00 million term loan due on 2027-09-24, under 10 months after the as-of date, with two one-year extension options at the issuer's discretion subject to conditions, then the USD 300.00 million loan due in April 2028, and a cost of debt that has already risen. If the 2027 term loan repriced to the 5.51% to 5.91% of the newer term loans from its 4.97% rate after hedges, annual interest would rise by USD 2.70 million to USD 4.70 million. No management outlook is supplied, so this view is the analyst's own and is not management's.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the 2029 stack is the issue: USD 689.40 million falls due in 2029 and extensions on the two term loans would move those maturities into 2029 and 2030, while the annual report states that operating cash flow is expected to repay only part of the debt at maturity. Sector tailwinds are an upcycle in lodging demand after a fall, and headwinds are inflation, tariffs and competition from non-traditional accommodation. Refinancing confidence rests on the 2026 completion of the USD 569.00 million and USD 150.00 million term loans, the unsecured structure and the par call on the 2029 notes from 2026-09-15, which lets the issuer refinance them early if markets allow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario repeats the FY2025 transmission on last-twelve-months figures; it is the analyst's judgement built on an observed year and is not a management case. The starting condition is a second fall in international, government, corporate and group travel. The first operating break is cost stickiness: in FY2025 property operating expenses rose while revenue fell, so reported EBITDA fell 8.23% and operating cash flow fell 14.58%. Applied to the last twelve months, EBITDA would fall to USD 301.99 million and operating cash flow to USD 232.89 million, net leverage would rise to 5.79x with cash interest unchanged and cover would fall to 2.69 times, or 2.52 times with a 100 bp rise on the unhedged floating debt, which the issuer sizes at USD 7.9 million a year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow less capex of USD 142.02 million would still cover distributions of USD 117.10 million 1.21 times with capex held at the last-twelve-months level, but only 0.91 times if capex returned to the USD 126.40 million of FY2025, so distributions or capex would have to give; liquidity of USD 1,048.34 million would be untouched, so the scenario does not lead to liquidity distress within the 2027 and 2028 maturities. Management levers are cutting capex, which fell 31.81% in the first nine months of 2026, reducing the common dividend, leaving the USD 250.00 million repurchase programme unused and applying the USD 90.00 million of sale cash to debt. The residual risk is the refinancing of the 2027 term loan in a weak earnings year, when leverage would be higher and the covenant tests, whose ratio values are not printed, could bind. Default is not assumed because the figures do not support it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, RLJ Lodging Trust presents an adequate business profile supported by 92 brand-affiliated, rooms-led hotels, no sponsor and a mostly unsecured structure, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 5.31x (5.04x pro forma for the 2026-10-08 sale), interest cover of 2.94 times and earnings that fall faster than revenue. Cash-flow durability appears adequate but thinner than the last twelve months suggest, because operating cash flow less capex covers distributions 1.55 times and capex is flexible, yet it covered them only 1.00 times in FY2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2026 earnings recovery holding through the 2027 term loan decision, the cost of replacing 4.00% notes in 2029 at rates near the 5.51% to 5.91% paid on the newest term loans, and the use of the sale proceeds. The primary downside path is a second demand fall like FY2025 that lifts leverage and cuts cover before the 2027 to 2029 maturities are refinanced. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant ratio values, ratings and prices, management guidance and a post-sale balance sheet. Fundamental credit synthesis completed. Top risk: refinancing the 2027 and 2028 term loans and the 2029 notes at higher cost on earnings that are still below FY2024.

fields.value: Liquidity is the strongest support. Cash and the undrawn revolver give USD 1,048.34 million, which funds the 2027 and 2028 term loans 1.31 times, and the 2026 refinancing pre-funded the notes due in 2026, so default probability over the next two years is low unless covenant compliance fails.

fields.value: The unsecured structure supports recovery for the unsecured debt: only eight hotels carry mortgage loans, the other hotels carry no mortgage, and the indenture and credit agreements test the unencumbered asset to debt ratio, so unsecured creditors keep access to most of the asset base, although their ranking among themselves is not stated.

fields.value: The 2026 operating recovery and cash conversion support deleveraging: comparable RevPAR rose 7.04% for nine months, reported EBITDA rose 5.26%, and operating cash flow less capex covers distributions 1.55 times with capex that can be cut, so net leverage can fall if the recovery holds and the sale cash repays debt.

fields.value: Hedging and an interest-only profile bound the rate risk: 65.7% of debt is fixed or effectively fixed and a 100 bp rise on the rest costs about USD 7.9 million a year, which is 7.05% of last-twelve-months cash interest, so a rate shock would slow cover but not threaten it alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage and cover are the main weakness. At 5.31x (5.04x pro forma for the 2026-10-08 sale) and 2.94 times they have not improved since FY2024, so an earnings decline moves leverage directly toward the covenant tests without a cushion that the filings let us measure.

fields.value: Concentration reduces flexibility: two managers run 51.09% of hotels, three brand families cover 83 of 93 hotels and three markets supplied 60.84% of the 2026 revenue growth, so a single manager, brand or region event reaches cash flow broadly.
